captions.t: In nineteen thirteen, a roulette wheel in Monte Carlo landed on black twenty-six times in a row.
After about fifteen blacks, gamblers rushed to bet on red. Surely red was due.
It wasn't. The ball has no memory. Every spin has the same odds. And people lost millions of francs that night.
It's called the gambler's fallacy. And it's not just casinos. People do it with stocks, crypto and even sports.
Past results don't change future odds. Follow for more money psychology.
